svg.title: Translation and signed scaling change centre and spread in different ways
svg.desc: The five unit-free codes are minus one, zero, one, two and three, with mean one and population variance two. Three decoding rules are plotted on the same centimetre measurement scale. Adding forty-five gives values forty-four through forty-eight, mean forty-six, variance two and standard deviation square root two. Decoding as forty-five plus four times the code gives forty-one, forty-five, forty-nine, fifty-three and fifty-seven, mean forty-nine, variance thirty-two and standard deviation four square root two. Decoding with negative four gives paired values forty-nine, forty-five, forty-one, thirty-seven and thirty-three, which must be reordered; the mean is forty-one and the spread is unchanged from positive four. Standard deviation uses the absolute scale factor; variance uses its square.
